title: Path analyzer, Test a list, PAC evaluation, what-if and the Data Flow Map: regression, Secure by Design and functional QA (cloud wave 6)

checks.what: Every connector forward method the SDK documents (ZIA, ECSELF, ZPA, ECZPA, DIRECT, LOCAL_SWITCH, PROXYCHAIN, DROP, INVALID, unknown) ends where it says
Connector group, source IP and groups, exclusion, destinations, ZPA pool, ZPA segments and groups, destination workload groups, unevaluated criteria
Workload group membership by tag: AND/OR within and across containers, tag types, untyped tags, any value, picked groups, empty and unreadable groups
Firewall network services and service groups: port ranges, TCP/UDP, ANY, predefined names, unresolved groups, source ports
Firewall network applications and app groups: well-known ports, unnamed ports, unknown applications, unresolved groups
Every firewall action and accessControl; no default rule read is unknown
Every DNS Control action (ALLOW, BLOCK, BLOCK_WITH_RESPONSE, REDIR_REQ, REDIR_RES, REDIR_ZPA, REDIR_REQ_DOH, REDIR_REQ_KEEP_SENDER, REDIR_REQ_TCP, REDIR_REQ_UDP)
DNS criteria incl. the DNS-over-HTTPS category, protocols in both spellings, query types, resolved categories, applications, destination groups
Sandbox per file type and protocol (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, FOHTTP, ANY), first-time action, threat class and score, encrypted traffic
File Type Control per file type, protocol and operation (UPLOAD, DOWNLOAD, UPLOAD_DOWNLOAD) and action
Data Flow Map counts for every platform x network: one class per path, sums equal traces, recount equals summary, high weak points
App profile choice: scoped profiles, rule order as numbers, IP bypasses, Z-Tunnel 2.0 packet tunnel lists, forwarding action shapes
PAC string methods, operators, values and classification against JavaScript; refusals for constructs outside the subset
What-if identity normalisation, matching by id, name and login, search bounds and errors, depends-on ranking
Test a list: headers and notes, bad blocks and ranges, lookup retries / quota / cap / halving with injected sleep, recommendations by area, Fix selected, exports, ICMP and any
HAR batch: one read, lookup chunks of 100 matched by url or position, errors per host, Stop keeps what was analyzed, cap
Kept reads from earlier versions (DLP rules without flags, app profiles without users or tunnel lists) still trace
Fixed-seed fuzz of wrong types in every firewall, DNS, Sandbox, ATP, connector, forwarding profile, app profile and identity field
IDN entries, non-ASCII digits, full-width names, IPv4-mapped IPv6
One analysis of 5,000 rules (spread, and on shared groups) and 5,000 connector rules under 2 s CPU
Test a list memory per row; MAX_ROWS boundary; parse cache bounded
Every failed read is recorded with a reason (never an empty list), never a 500; ZPA read errors masked
Markdown export escapes tenant strings; CSV export neutralises formulas
PAC evaluation never resolves or fetches; an injected resolver is the only DNS; identity search reaches one fixed endpoint
Lookup and module errors in job results are covered by the existing token-echo canary (tests/test_secret_canaries.py); identity search never repeats exception text
Nothing in scope, ZIA not in scope for a list, channel other than web: refused before any read
PAC number literals with an exponent (1e21) and the NaN name are refused, not evaluated (fail closed)
Host names are never resolved: IP-based rules for a host name are unknown, or an assumption stated
ssl_flow._names / _sort_key on wrong-type rule fields (outside these files)

findings.title: An IPv4 a-b range compared with an IPv6 address raised TypeError: the analysis (and a Test a list run) failed for an IPv6 destination or source
findings.fix: Ranges compare only addresses of their own family (zia_path_modules._ip_rel, workload_path._ip_in)

findings.title: A firewall network-application rule was a definite no match on a port no service names (SSH on TCP/2222): a definite allow ZIA would not give
findings.fix: On an unnamed port a network application criterion is unknown (conditional), never no match

findings.title: DNS rule protocols in the SDK docstring's spelling (UDP, TCP, DOHTTPS) were not recognised: answers falsely conditional
findings.fix: UDP and UDP_RULE both match the assumed UDP lookup

findings.title: A DNS rule on an IP destination group was always unknown, even with the group read by the Cloud Firewall
findings.fix: DNS rules use the destination groups the firewall read (same /ipDestinationGroups list, same scope)

findings.title: Sandbox and FTC criteria took a bare extension (pdf) as a ZIA file category: a definite no match
findings.fix: Only FTCATEGORY_* values are file types, as in data_flow.trace

findings.title: A network service limited to a source port was a definite match on its destination port
findings.fix: Such a service is unknown when its destination port matches

findings.title: A File Type Control rule for UPLOAD_DOWNLOAD did not apply to an upload or a download: a configured block reported as no rule
findings.fix: UPLOAD_DOWNLOAD applies to UPLOAD and DOWNLOAD (the value pack_channels validates)

findings.title: A connector rule restricted to destination workload groups (destWorkloadGroups) was evaluated as unrestricted: a definite DIRECT
findings.fix: destWorkloadGroups is a criterion not evaluated: the rule is conditional

findings.title: sourceIpGroupExclusion was ignored: a rule for sources outside its groups was applied to sources inside them
findings.fix: With sourceIpGroupExclusion the source must be outside every group (assumed from the SDK field); unknown members stay unknown

findings.title: A forwarding rule with method INVALID or an unknown one was reported as forwarded to ZIA (fail open)
findings.fix: An unknown forward method decides 'unknown' with an impact, never ZIA

findings.title: A connector ZPA rule missed a renamed segment named by ZPA id; an empty segment-group name matched every groupless segment
findings.fix: All ids (id, externalId, zpaId) are compared; empty names and ids never match

findings.title: PAC string methods diverged from JavaScript (lastIndexOf fromIndex ignored, indexOf('', n), Infinity positions refused)
findings.fix: ECMAScript ToIntegerOrInfinity and clamping for every position

findings.title: Test a list kept one answer per row: about 800 bytes a row, 201 MB for 250,000 rows
findings.fix: Rows with the same answer share one kept evaluation, without another row's headline (36 MB for 250,000 rows)

findings.title: A group- or user-scoped Client Connector app profile was taken as every user's (sample iOS profile is for Drivers): a definite path
findings.fix: A scoped profile ahead of the first unscoped one that treats the destination differently makes the path depend on the user (unverified), naming each profile

findings.title: A connector rule, workload group or IP group list field of the wrong type raised TypeError (fixed-seed fuzz)
findings.fix: One list guard: a list is a list, one string is one item, anything else is nothing

findings.title: App profiles sorted by ruleOrder as text ('10' before '9': wrong profile); mixed types and odd systemProxyData raised errors
findings.fix: ruleOrder is compared as a number (anything else sorts last); systemProxyData must be an object

findings.title: A URL lookup answer with categories of the wrong type raised TypeError (single, HAR batch, list); a string was split into letters
findings.fix: One shared parser (path_analyzer.labels / lookup_answer)

findings.title: 5,000 firewall rules on shared groups took 3.4 s per analysis (indexes rebuilt and addresses re-parsed per rule)
findings.fix: Indexes built once per evaluation; address entries parsed once (bounded cache, long strings never cached): 0.7 s

findings.title: data_flow.load_packs opened each pack's policy file without closing it
findings.fix: Read with a context manager

findings.title: 5,000 connector forwarding rules on shared groups took 4 s (indexes, parses and lower-casing redone per rule)
findings.fix: Built once per evaluation: 0.6 s

findings.title: Test a list scanned every address entry for every row: 223 us a row against a 5,000-network group
findings.fix: The address space is split at every range end; a row is one bisect and each stretch's entries are worked out once (39 us a row); a property test checks it against a full scan

findings.title: A list port of '²' raised a bare ValueError (HTTP 500 with a trace); '٣' was taken as a port and as the PAC number 3
findings.fix: Every digit check is ASCII only

findings.title: A tenant list entry written in Unicode never matched its IDN destination (placed in punycode): a Block rule reported as not applying
findings.fix: Every list matcher (and Test a list's index) normalises entries with zia_path_modules.entry_host

findings.title: The app profile's IP bypasses were never compared with the destination: 10.1.2.3 (excluded 10.0.0.0/8) reported tunnelled and enforced
findings.fix: An IP destination inside one is bypassed with the entry named; a host name exclusion bypasses that host; public IP bypasses on a host name are stated as an assumption

findings.title: Z-Tunnel 2.0 packet tunnel exclusions and inclusions were never read: an excluded address was reported tunnelled to ZIA
findings.fix: Read from the app profile and applied when the network's mode is Z-Tunnel 2.0; also counted when a scoped profile differs

findings.title: ssl_flow._names and _sort_key crash on rule fields of the wrong type: a hostile snapshot fails the Path analyzer and Data Flow Map
findings.fix: Treat one string as one item and anything else that is not a list as none; an id that is not a number sorts as 0
findings.proposed_patch:
diff --git a/ssl_flow.py b/ssl_flow.py
index ca86a6e..690a573 100644
--- a/ssl_flow.py
+++ b/ssl_flow.py
@@ -111,7 +111,9 @@ def _f(r: Dict[str, Any], *names: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
 
 def _names(items: Any) -> List[str]:
     out: List[str] = []
-    for x in items or []:
+    # A tenant list of the wrong type: one string is one item; anything else
+    # that is not a list (a number, true) is no item, never a crash.
+    for x in ([items] if isinstance(items, str) else items if isinstance(items, (list, tuple)) else []):
         if isinstance(x, dict):
             v = x.get("name") or x.get("id") or x.get("url")
             if v is not None:
@@ -290,7 +292,11 @@ def _sort_key(rule: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
     except (TypeError, ValueError):
         o = 10 ** 6
     # The default rule is always evaluated last whatever its order says.
-    return (1 if rule.get("default_rule") else 0, o, int(rule.get("id") or 0))
+    try:
+        rid = int(rule.get("id") or 0)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        rid = 0
+    return (1 if rule.get("default_rule") else 0, o, rid)
 
 
 # ── Tenant reads ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
